source.title: Mixed Precision Scaling Laws for Quantized Pretraining
source.authors: Jinuk Kim; R. Saha; Muhammed Fatih Balin; Youngsuk Park

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no material truncation or garbling noted.
record.tranche_reason: The study fits and evaluates scaling laws for held-out pretraining loss and extrapolation, using quantized-pretraining grids and a modified law rather than directly reproducing the original studies' setups.
record.gate_note: Table 1's recipe comparisons measure loss changes at one model size and token budget, not a scaling relation, so they are not separate claim-version rows. Cited results from other work are not recorded. Figure 1's precision-allocation result is recorded separately from the parameter/token trend.
record.test_reason: The study fits power-law loss laws, with BF16 baseline coefficients shared, to new quantized-pretraining grids (Llama 30M–200M; Qwen3 280M–910M). It evaluates held-out extrapolation to larger models and token budgets and compares law forms. That is a new setting with results on V1, V2 and V7. I chose T3 rather than the reader's T2 because the setting, quantized training, is the new element; the method of fitting and extrapolating loss laws is the standard one.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that modelling persistent forward and backward quantization error yields a law that predicts held-out quantized-pretraining loss better than existing laws, with up to 11× lower MSE. Keeping the first and last blocks in higher precision is especially effective in the backward pass. The law predicts that compute-optimal precision rises with budget, with the forward pass getting higher precision first.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops a quantized-pretraining law with effective parameter/data counts and separate persistent-error terms, then tests extrapolation on Qwen3 and published Quartet grids. It is not a direct reproduction of the original full-precision scaling-law experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Fitted exponents vary between Quartet and Qwen3 grids and between model-size and data extrapolation fits. Held-out MSE also changes when persistent-error terms or the data-rescaling dependence are changed. Layer-mixing prediction varies with pass and block-selection strategy.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the fitted law and an assumed hardware cost model, the compute-optimal fraction of NVFP4 blocks falls as the compute budget grows. The backward pass keeps NVFP4 to larger budgets than the forward pass.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: With persistent quantization error, compute-optimal training precision increases with compute budget.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing the persistent forward-error term raises the geometric-mean held-out MSE about 3×. Quantized loss thus has a scale-independent floor above E.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Quantized pretraining adds an irreducible loss term that is not offset by more parameters or data.

record.problems: The extrapolation tests cover limited size and token-budget ranges rather than orders of magnitude. The compute-optimal allocation is produced by numerical optimization of the fitted law and an assumed hardware cost model, not validated against independently trained compute-optimal runs. Reported fit metrics have no uncertainty intervals.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted under the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Several orders of magnitude in N, D or compute. The fits span at most about 7× in N (30M–200M) and 32× in tokens per parameter. There is no compute-axis law.
Extrapolation by orders of magnitude. The held-out targets are only 1.2–2× beyond the calibration range.
Power-law exponents of N* and D* versus compute. Optima are computed from the fitted law, with no empirical validation and no stated exponents.
Not tested. Depth and width are tied to each other in the Qwen3-derived configs.
Not tested. There are no other modalities, no repeated-data regime and no fine-tuning or transfer.
Not tested. There is no downstream evaluation; only C4 validation loss is reported.
Curve bending away from a single power law at larger scale, and parameter-counting or schedule effects, were not tested.

missing.what: Held-out MSE for all 14 law-form combinations: error terms inside vs outside γ, ρD dependence, and which ε terms are included. Placing the ε terms inside γ raises MSE 1.31× on average.
Per-panel fitted γS and held-out R² for layer-mixed fits (0.979–0.997 with the proposed endpoints vs 0.962–0.984 with Quartet endpoints)
Optimal N and tokens per parameter stay nearly unchanged under assumed MXFP8 speedups of 1.6× and 1.4× (figure only)

record.verdict_notes: I dropped the reader's V3 limits_scope label: missing exponents make V3 untested, not a scope limit, and the optima are model-derived rather than measured. Rows r5–r12 and r15–r19 compare the study's own law with another law; I kept them because the law itself is the object of the claim. Setup details that may affect the exponents: CompleteP parameterization; learning rate scaled as D^-0.32; token budgets obtained by resuming warmup-stable-decay runs before the decay phase; N counted as non-embedding parameters; C4 validation loss.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests fitted loss scaling in quantized-pretraining grids and fits BF16 baselines, but not a general law across several orders of magnitude in model size, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolations are to a 200M model from 30M–100M models, a 910M model from 280M–640M models, or the largest tested token budget. It does not test extrapolations orders of magnitude larger.
The study numerically optimizes model size, tokens, and precision under its cost model, but does not fit or report power-law exponents for optimal parameter count and token count versus compute.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities, repeated-data regime, fine-tuning, or transfer setting.
The study tests fitting choices and variation across its quantized-pretraining grids, but not the full range of original-law disagreements or systematic curve bending away from power laws.

conditions.value: optimal configuration switches toward MXFP8 as budget increases

rows.measure: Optimal precision allocation versus compute budget
rows.value: The optimal configuration switches to MXFP8 in the forward pass around C0 = 1020 FLOPs and in both passes at around C0 = 5 × 1022 FLOPs.
rows.note: The text also reports a gradual backward transition. This is a result about optimal precision allocation, not the parameter/token power trends in V3.

relationships.condition: Choice of fitting subset, data grid and law form in quantized pretraining
relationships.reason: Exponents shift with the calibration split on the same grid (α 0.622 vs 0.701) and across grids (γ 0.32 vs 0.77) (r1–r4). Changing the law form changes held-out MSE by up to 11×, and the Quartet form systematically underestimates held-out loss (r5, r6, r14–r19).
relationships.display_finding: Changing calibration splits shifted α from 0.622 to 0.701, changing grids shifted γ from 0.32 to 0.77, and changing law form altered held-out MSE by up to 11×; Quartet systematically underestimated held-out loss.
